analyst_view.overall: Atalanta have not won in six games in all competitions and have conceded 15 in their last six; several Italian outlets say Maurizio Sarri's job could depend on this derby, though the club has so far backed him. Ivan Juric faces his former club with Monza third from bottom after three straight league defeats, and he said he went home 'angry, mainly with myself' after losing to Bologna. Atalanta are still missing Hien, Kossounou, Bellanova, Kristensen, Raspadori, Gaetano and Pompei, but Kessié and Kolasinac are back; for Monza, Birindelli is out while Pessina is available.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals. Atalanta's attack has stalled (no goal at home to Parma, a late Krstovic equaliser against Kairat), but their patched defence has conceded 15 in six and has faded in second halves, and Monza have scored 11 in their last six. These cancel out, so we stay with the model.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners. Juric's Monza press man-to-man and Sarri's Atalanta like long spells of possession, which roughly balance each other. Nothing in the news moves us away from the model.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.3 cards. This is a Lombardy derby against Juric's former club, both teams are under pressure, and Juric's aggressive man-marking against an Atalanta side short of first-choice defenders is likely to produce fouls. That points to a scrappier game than the model has.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.1 shots. Both sides want the ball high up the pitch, but Atalanta are low on confidence. We see no clear reason to move far from the model.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.3 shots on target, which is high. Atalanta's attack has been blunt lately, and Monza's support for Varela is still undecided between Mota Carvalho, Robinson and Zeballos, so we expect slightly fewer efforts on target.
